ch: Choose TWO of these words: enormous, fragile, generous. Write one sentence for each word with a clue in the same sentence that helps a reader guess its meaning. Underline your clue.
N: To panic is to suddenly feel so afraid that you cannot think clearly.
Hints are small pieces of help that point you towards an answer.
A definition tells you exactly what a word means, like the drought example.
Immediately = straight after, with nothing in between.
A synonym is a word with the same or a very similar meaning (famished = very hungry). Antonyms are opposites.
Because gives the reason: it works the same way for this reason.
Familiar = known to you. The writer adds an easier word you already know.
Opposite = as different as possible (hot / cold). Unlike, but and while signal a contrast.
A reader infers a meaning from clues. Careful: a writer implies, a reader infers.
Suggests = points towards something without saying it directly.
However introduces a contrast: after the good news, a warning.
Reliable = you can trust it to be right every time.
Vague = not clear or not detailed. The opposite of precise.
Replacing A with B = putting B in the place of A.
We say replace something WITH something else.
Probably = likely, but not certain.
Read further = continue reading the next part.
Finally introduces the last point of the article.
To spot something = to notice or see it.
A detective solves a case = finds the answer to a mystery.
